questions.key_step: Equal projections on three vectors give two linear equations; solve for the direction.
questions.justification: Linear system from equal projections, no insight needed beyond the definition; direct check against options.

questions.key_step: Expand $(a-c)\times b$ and dot with $a$ to kill $a\times b$.
questions.justification: One familiar triple-product trick applied once; a long computation is avoided entirely.

questions.key_step: Apply the skew-line shortest-distance formula.
questions.justification: A direct formula with one cross product and a dot product, nothing to decide.

questions.key_step: $v_1\perp v_2$ so the requested sum is $|v|^2$ once $\lambda$ is found.
questions.justification: Find $\lambda$ from the angle, then resolve into components (or use Pythagoras); three or four routine steps.

questions.key_step: $\hat a\times\hat b$ is perpendicular to both unit vectors, so it drops out of each dot product.
questions.justification: Chain of dot products with a cosine from $\sin^{-1}$; routine multi-step, one orthogonality idea.

questions.key_step: Point on the line fixes $c,d$; direction perpendicular to both lines gives two linear equations.
questions.justification: Several routine stages (point on line, two dot conditions, linear system) without any new idea.

questions.key_step: $|a+b|=2P\cos(\theta/2)$, $|a-b|=2P\sin(\theta/2)$ turns the ratio into $\tan(\pi/4+\theta/2)$.
questions.justification: Half-angle form of the magnitudes plus recognising $\tan(\pi/4+x)$; a moderately less common trigonometric recognition, but short.

questions.key_step: Area $=\frac12\cdot QR\cdot PM$ with $PM$ the perpendicular distance from $P$ to the line.
questions.justification: One familiar move (distance of a point from a line) and the area formula; options in $m,n$ only re-state the ratio.

questions.key_step: de Gua's theorem for a right-angled tetrahedron corner.
questions.justification: One well-known result applied once.

questions.key_step: Axis-parallel lines: shortest distance is $|\lambda-1|$; distance of the point from $L_1$ in the $xy$-plane.
questions.justification: Two routine uses of distance formulas with an ordering condition on $\lambda$.

questions.key_step: Collinearity of $P,A,B$ with two independent parameters, then a determinant.
questions.justification: Two parameters, two nonlinear cross-multiplied equations with a spurious root, then a $3\times3$ determinant; casework on precision.

questions.key_step: $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1$ with $\beta=\gamma=\alpha/2$ and the half-angle identity.
questions.justification: Direction-cosine identity plus half-angle identity and range of angles; short but needs both ideas.

questions.key_step: Foot of perpendicular, then the two points at distance $2\sqrt{17}$ and a dot product.
questions.justification: Foot, two points, dot product: routine chain of three stages with exact arithmetic; options help check.

questions.key_step: Only the angle at $A$ matters: $\text{Area}=\frac12\,AB\cdot AC\sin\theta$.
questions.justification: Find $A$, angle between the lines, area formula; routine three-stage chain.

questions.key_step: Feet from $(1,1,1)$-direction conditions, then cross product for the area.
questions.justification: Two feet, a cross product and an area; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Dot product gives a quadratic in $\lambda$; compare its roots with $[-1,3]$.
questions.justification: Single expansion and a quadratic; the only care is the range check (and an expansion slip is easy).

questions.key_step: $Q=P+\lambda d$ with $QR=5$ gives $\lambda=2$ (discard $\lambda=0$); then area from a cross product.
questions.justification: Quadratic with a discarded trivial root, then cross product; routine chain of four stages.

questions.key_step: $E$ foot of altitude: $AE^2=AD^2-h^2$ with $h$ from the volume; $E$ on the median with the correct sign.
questions.justification: Four stages (area, height from volume, Pythagoras, point on median with sign choice) and exact fractions with square roots.

questions.key_step: Arc ratio $\Rightarrow$ central angles $15^\circ,75^\circ$; dot the vector equation with $\overrightarrow{OA}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}$.
questions.justification: Combines arc/angle geometry with vector components and $15^\circ$ trigonometric values; two linked ideas and surd arithmetic.

questions.key_step: $\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OA}=\frac{r}{r+1}\,\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OQ}$ turns both terms into functions of $r$.
questions.justification: Section formula, a cross product and a dot product, then a quadratic in $r$; routine but long.
